resources.string: Hold volume down at the lowest media volume for finer, quieter steps, or volume up at the highest for a boost.

Volume Zoom watches only the volume keys. Hold volume down at the lowest media step to zoom into 10 quieter steps, or hold volume up at the highest step to zoom into 10 steps of boost (software gain on the media output). No other input or screen content is read.
Volume Zoom is off. In Accessibility → Volume Zoom, turn on \"Use Volume Zoom\". Leave \"Volume Zoom shortcut\" off: it only adds a floating button, and the volume keys work without it.

If Android says \"App was denied access\" when you turn it on: open App info, tap ⋮ (top right), choose \"Allow restricted settings\" and turn it on again. Android only shows that option after it has blocked the switch once. It applies to apps installed from a file, not to ones from an app store such as F-Droid.

Quieter: lower media volume to its last step, then hold volume down to zoom in (starts at 0 dB). Each down press is one fine step quieter, and up steps back out. A fresh press on the last fine step mutes.
Louder: at the top media step, hold volume up to zoom into boost (starts at 0 dB). Each up press adds gain, and down steps back out. A hold that starts below the top step never boosts.
Quick presses at either end behave as usual.
Deepest fine step: −%1$d dB (%2$.1f dB per step)
Loudest boost step: +%1$d dB (%2$.1f dB per step)
Hold time to zoom in: %1$d ms
Volume keys control media when nothing is playing (Pixel default; turn off if idle keys change the ringer)
